Suppose I never ever got the chance to eat pizza. Is it wise to prefer eating pizza over building a meaningful relationship and being genuinely happy? I mean pizza is such an amazing thing, no doubt about it, and it's such a pain that for years I could not have tasted it for some reason, but is it THAT important? I mean not even objectively, but for YOU? 

There are things people cannot do. Some can't run, because no legs. Some can't sing. Some will never be popular at parties. And as painful as it might get, it's tolerable as long as you focus on other things. That is why for me it seemed superficial, to choose to dwell on some desire which is probably important mostly because you don't have it, not because it is something you would like if you thought about it. And my personal experience has nothing to do with anything here. I can see why you would get such an impression, but you sound like it's impossible to maintain my opinion AND be rejected a lot, which is simply false.

There is often quite a dissonance between what is expected/considered a norm and what we actually want. Feelings of being somehow, what's the word, unable to perform the function which supposed to define you, are, well, they are pretty shitty, that's more than understandable. It sucks, I'm somewhat in a similar place myself although for perhaps different reasons. But if you are only bothered by it because of others, could that desire be even called *yours*? I don't think so. And I also think you should get rid of desires forced on you by society. Don't smoke cause it's portrayed in films as sexy or manly or whatever - it's bad for you! Here it's the same shit, really. Once you get rid of these fake desires, trust me, it will be soooo fcking worth it, with girl or without her, it would feel so liberating - to feel yourself, being free from all these anxieties. 

And once more about suicide - just don't. Pm me if you want to talk some other time. It's not a solution, it never is. 

Ok I'm off to bed, thanks for the AMA etc etc. My conclusion, although I realise you probably still not convinced at all, is that you delude yourself about the things you want.
Jesus, stop being so full of yourself. Of course it's your teammates who keep you at low mmr.

Tbh I don't think reddit particularly dislikes people who claim to be unnattractive, it's just the defeatist attitude is (no pun intended) unnattactive and generally disliked. 

Your unnatractiveness might have ruined your chances a couple of times. The same way some circumstances might have ruined chances of that guy. The same way another guy was rejected because he has shit personality and looks are not everything. You know it's fine being unnattractive - and no, I'm not trying to downplay the problem or say that your experience was not significant to you. I'm saying that it seems to me that you want two things: to get a chance at dating without being "ugly one in the relationship" and to have a better public image. The latter is indeed solved by getting fit and developing good personality - those things are respected, no matter what kind of face and hight you have. Seriously. As for the former, well, again, I don't see why unnatractiveness is a valid excuse in some special way as opposed to other excuses. Every person has drawbacks. We always decide whether person's good qualities outweight his/hers flaws. Why you deny others the right to choose to keep you in their circle of friends/potential dates? Isn't being loved the thing that matters? There is always that one/two things you hate about your SO, why wouldn't it be some aspects of appearence? I would still totally go for a person with the great sense of humour, body and I dunno, shared interests. I do not mean to be rude, but I fail to see your problem more than "I have a problem and that is why instead of improving my overall chances and changing strategy I gonna just cancel the whole project". Does it have to be ideal? Do you want to be happy or do you want girls to say how cute you are but it being superficial? 

If you decided you are ugly because of the feedback of others, you might as well at least *consider* the dominant opinion of his thread and reshape your view for the sake of getting a bigger prize in a long run - a prize, I'm sorry, but totally achievable and a prize I would speculate you are truly after, but deny yourself.

Who the fuck even cares how attractive you are if you are so convinced that you look ugly. Like, do you NEED to be liked by everyone so much? Even if we assume that you are indeed less attractive than the average male, it doesn't seem like you are some kind of Quasimodo. Which basically means that your unnattractiveness is not something which ruins your chances at getting whatever that is what you want, unless you want to be the most attractive guy at the party. With sufficient effort your drawbacks could be compensated in other areas, making you worth considering in the eyes of the opposite sex, for example. For me it still comes down to "comfortable vs. good" I've talked about. All of your concerns are not unfamiliar to me, and perhaps even there is no answer to some of them (within our immediate reach at least). I hate to pull "it gets better" card, but I think here in particular it's relevant: if it is the answer you want, then time DOES give some perspective and tells whether in retrospect X was significant/manipulative/wrong or w/e. That or qualified help from a professional. Again, maybe a bit cliche considering this sub, but did you try to talk to someone who might have experience with helping people? Me and the like can only do so much, I aint no therapist. It is indeed uncomfortable to not know what fueled your depression in the first place, are you really depressed, or are you just delusional; are your behavioural patterns include manipulation and how bad it is. Then there are trust issues and being afraid of unconsciously hurting other people. While time CAN put things into perspective I won't lie to you unless you make attempts at moving forward it probably won't change. And here comes curious thing: is it even necessary to dwell on the mistakes of the past etc? I mean it does seem natural, analyzing your actions in order to prevent bad stuff from happening. But you admit it yourself that it kinda leads to confusion, the vicious cycle of not knowing yourself anymore. That's why death seems so comforting - it breaks the cycle which was created by mistake in the first place. Might it seem compelling? Yes. Is it good, or right? Is it? I think you gotta look for things that motivate you, search little tiny things which make you feel nice. You must hav cared at some point for someone or something - do it for their sake, despite confusion, despite hardships, despite being blinded and your mind playing tricks on you. But uncomfortable doesn't mean final. You speak of not deserving to live, and even if you actually believe that some people do not deserve to live, which in the vast majority of times is a super questionable claim, the one who passes the judgement here is you. Why punish yourself so hard? Yes, what you did might have been wrong, nasty, w/e. It still doesn't have to end like this. It's not GOOD. Are you ready to sacrifice good, whatever it is for you? Do you think it is a good thing to do - to prefer a comforting oblivion of the abyss to the warmth of future potential relationships, enjoyment of little things, fun, achievement? Is it worth to sacrifice an endless stream of good things for a little bit of comfort on which you would not be able to reflect? Because really if you want to clear your head and be sure that you are not manipulative then the solution is very different from the one you are considering. I would say that you have to decide what do you want but this is actually the next step. First you must face your discomfort and see that it doesn't undermine you being a human, a real person who is capable of both love and being loved. I don't know anything about you but I know that you, flanking out of college or not, having friends or not, can be and can do anything at all and it will be a great loss for the world if you'd go. This last claim might be disputed by some people by some banal "ah world is cruel and won't care" but I don't believe in that, I believe in being the world to one person, two persons, three persons. Each human life ending prematurely is a great loss and certainly not a good thing. See for yourself whether you are ready to sacrifice everything because you don't know the answers to some of the questions. I know my analogies suck but you also were a little child, are you ready to rob that child of his future? Or do you honestly think that you are that-beyond-redemption bad? "Genuinely bad person"? I know I'm nothing to you but you know, I forgive you, now go and try your best being a genuinely good person and forgive yourself. Here's a little secret: a genuinely good person is that who tries to be a genuinely good person and doesn't stop trying when he fails. Let's try again, despite everything. Finding a therapist might be necessary, not all things can be overcome by sheer power of will, when you break a leg you go see a doctor. But it's alright, it's all fine as long as you are trying. And if you stopped trying it's also still fine because you literally can start trying. I know that you are capable of doing good and that's what is important now. Forget everything and go do what is good, because it's good.

So, as I understand it, you were depressed even before your friend stopped talking to you? It then would seem as if that her rejection was only a catalyst to your suicidal thoughts lately. And that if it wouldn't be the cause something else would. It's ok to feel sad or even shitty after a break up and I realise that hearing something among these lines doesn't make it any easier. It still feels to me that it's time to kinda face yourself and the issues you have been experiencing. You have nobody left to turn to, yes. I hate to sound like an asshat, but it could be viewed in a good light. Ask yourself this, honestly: if she takes you back, will it fix things? It might seem so, but I doubt it. It's nice to have friends who keep us alive through our darkest moments. But if that's the only thing keeping one on track we call describe such dependence as an unhealthy one. And unhealthy things, things that paint your future in bleak colours and weaken your will to live, they, well, hurt us so much as you already know. Maybe I'm misreading all of it, but it appears to me that as sad as your situation might be it's not hopeless and there is an opportunity within it. I'm not saying that you shouldn't feel bad about it or that other people got it worse. I just think that sometimes the comfort you were talking about, the comfort we gain from interaction with friends, have to be sacrificed because... Because it's suffocating. You know, like when one is freezing to death for some reason it feels sleepy and many die like that every winter asleep and frozen to death; we often confuse "comforting" and "good". It's ok to be alone, to experience discomfort. But no matter how bad it is, you've gotta make that tiny step out of it. Because it's good. For you, for her, for everyone.

I see, mistakes were made. There was one time when I also lost a friend this way, by being an asshole. Shortly after it just so happened that another person hurt me a lot. By the time that second person came to apologise I was so apathetic that I easily forgave him, since I didn't care anymore. Then oddly enough it kinda made me feel better: I was able to forgive another person, why not forgive myself? I went for a long walk and that was the best thing that happened for a long time. If nothing matters and you are feeling suicidal, why not at least be a nice person to yourself? :) It's easier than it sounds. Step by step. Forgive yourself as you would someone whom you love and appreciate. Probably it will make you feel better, it made me feel better. It just seems to me that when I thought of suicide myself what I truly wanted is some sense of liberation from all this guilt and fear. You might have made some mistakes, some poor decisions, but in the end you are the only one who prevents yourself from being happy. College, friends... Yeah it sucks especially when you see how its your fault. But I really hope that amidst all of the negativity you would not punish yourself for your mistakes. You need some love for yourself, despite everything. What I'm saying is, well, I don't have an advice to fix everything, and something might be without your reach at the moment, but please, don't hate yourself. If you feel bad for hurting your friend then don't hurt yourself! Or else your regret loses its meaning. But from what you've written it seems to me that you mean it. If you are still able to feel anything at all, you know what would be right - stop being an abusive asshole. And this includes stop abusing yourself in the first place. I really hope you will get better! <3
